newsitem.title: GREECE: CYPRUS TO LIBERALISE FOREIGN INVESTMENT - FIN MIN.
newsitem.headline: CYPRUS TO LIBERALISE FOREIGN INVESTMENT - FIN MIN.

text.p: Cyprus is planning to lift foreign investment controls and allow locals to invest in foreign companies, Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou told reporters in Athens during a roadshow by the Cyprus stock exchange.
"The further liberalisation of Cypriot investments in publicly-held companies abroad is being planned in the near future," Christodoulou said.
Under the current status quo listed investment companies and insurance firms are allowed to invest up to 20 percent of their assets abroad.
Cyprus intends to harmonise its economy with the EU and will be also introducing a gradual lifting of foreign exchange controls, he said.

"The government of Cyprus has decided to proceed with the gradual liberalisation of the credit system and policy affecting foreign investment in Cyprus as well as Cypriot investments abroad," the minister said.
Presently, foreign investors are allowed stakes up to 49 percent in Cypriot publicly held companies listed on the exchange with the exception of banks where the upper limit is 15 percent.

Christodoulou noted that Cyprus' economy had achieved an average real GDP growth rate of 4.5 percent during 1992-96 coupled with a low inflation rate of 3.0 percent -- indicators which compare favourably with those of other EU countries.

Foreign exchange reserves have reached a very satisfactory #2.3 billion providing import cover of about 15 months while the country's longer term foreign debt does not exceed 20 percent of GDP, he said.

The country's export orientation which has recently placed emphasis on the service sector is the driving force behind economic growth. It will play a more important role as Cyprus seeks to become a full member of the European Union.

"The stock exchanges of Greece and Cyprus have a good cooperation which should be further strengthened to help them flourish in the wider region," Christodoulou said. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
